prerequisites.title: Gusto Developer Account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up before filing the Production Pre-Approval.

prerequisites.title: Security documentation ready
prerequisites.detail: Have audits (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS), penetration test reports, policies and security contacts. Without a formal audit, Gusto asks for details on controls like MFA and encryption.

steps.title: Create Gusto Developer Account
steps.detail: Sign up in the Gusto Developer Portal.
steps.done_when: You can log in to the Developer Portal.

steps.title: Prepare security and use-case material
steps.detail: Draft the use-case description and collect policies, audit reports, pen test reports and contacts in the form Gusto asks for.
steps.done_when: All documents and contacts are ready to paste or upload.

steps.title: File Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: Submit the application and the security details before building.

steps.title: Wait for Partnerships and Security Review
steps.detail: No action is needed unless Gusto asks for more information, which puts the review on hold until you respond.
steps.done_when: Gusto emails next steps (direct) or notifies your Unified API partner.

steps.title: Build and test in demo environment
steps.detail: Supply a redirect URI to get the client ID and secret, and test all assigned scopes against api.gusto-demo.com.
steps.done_when: Integration works end to end in demo.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret, using the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Pass QA and get production credentials
steps.detail: After QA, Gusto issues production credentials via the Developer Portal. Production calls then go to api.gusto.com.
steps.done_when: Production credentials appear in the Developer Portal.

traps.title: The rate limit is evaluated over a 60-second rolling
traps.detail: The rate limit is evaluated over a 60-second rolling window per OAuth grant, so up to 200 requests are allowed in any 60-second window for each grant's access_token.

traps.title: Gusto assigns your scopes
traps.detail: Scopes are assigned during review by use case, and calls outside them are rejected in production. Extra scopes can only be requested after production release.

traps.title: No production test accounts
traps.detail: All testing before and after launch must happen in the demo environment.

traps.title: One OAuth grant per company
traps.detail: Since v2023-05-01, a token covers one company, so multi-company admins must authorize each company separately.

traps.title: Production redirect changes need support
traps.detail: Demo redirect URIs can be edited in the portal, but production ones need an email to Gusto. Wildcards and fragments are not allowed.

traps.title: Short token life and rate limit
traps.detail: Access tokens expire after 2 hours. The limit is 200 requests per minute per OAuth grant, and excess requests get HTTP 429.

blockers.what_it_means: Gusto asked for more information and is waiting for your response.
blockers.what_to_do: Watch for Gusto's request and reply quickly with the missing documents.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft responses and assemble the requested documents.

blockers.what_it_means: You may be calling outside your assigned scopes, or you do not have production credentials yet.
blockers.what_to_do: Confirm approval and stay within assigned scopes; contact Gusto to change scopes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare your API calls with the assigned scopes.

evidence.quote: composio_url = "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback"
evidence.answer: The callback URL that the redirect proxy forwards to on Composio's side is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack (general statement, not specific to Gusto, which the page does not mention).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: For managed toolkits, the developer does not need to register their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: Bring-your-own option: a custom auth config lets the developer supply their own OAuth app or other credentials for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available (general, for all toolkits).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps: they share quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed auth: it enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not include everything a developer needs (for example, write access to a specific Google API).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With managed apps, users see Composio's name on the OAuth consent screen rather than the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: In production, users should see the developer's app name instead of Composio, which is the most common reason to switch to a custom app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still [white-label the Connect Link page](/docs/authentication/white-labeling-authentication#customizing-the-connect-link) with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: A developer can still white-label the Connect Link page with their logo and app title without their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
evidence.answer: A custom auth config can be created for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances even when a managed app exists.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You don't have to pick one approach for all toolkits.
evidence.answer: Managed and custom approaches can be mixed: each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
